recentItems.title: PARIS ON LOCKDOWN? Police Seal Streets as Riots Shake France | ET Now | World News | Breaking News
recentItems.description:
Police deployed across central Paris on Monday night as an overnight curfew came into force following days of violent unrest in France. Footage showed police vans blocking roads, officers establishing security cordons, deserted public spaces and a helicopter searchlight sweeping across the city. According to the supplied report, around 2,400 people were arrested and nearly 1,000 police officers and gendarmes were injured nationwide, while hundreds of businesses were looted or damaged. The unrest also included burning barricades, torched vehicles and a fire that gutted a historic town hall in Limoges. The demonstrations began amid public anger over rising living costs and deteriorating school conditions, with more than 500,000 people reportedly taking to the streets. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the destruction and vowed a tough response. The partial Paris curfew ran from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., while République metro station was closed at police request.

recentItems.title: FICO EXPOSES EU’S “HYPOCRISY”! Russian Energy Row Erupts Over Billions for Ukraine | ET Now
recentItems.description:
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico criticised what he described as double standards in European policy towards Russia, questioning why Slovakia faces pressure over Russian energy imports while the United States moves to resume Russian diesel purchases and European countries continue buying Russian liquefied natural gas. Speaking at the Mochovce Nuclear Power Plant on Monday, Fico also challenged Ukraine's request for an additional €70 billion in European funding, arguing that Kyiv would struggle to repay previous financial support. He cited the removal of Russian sable furs from an EU sanctions list and repeated allegations concerning the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions. Fico's comments come amid disagreements within the European Union over further assistance to Ukraine and continued Russian energy imports. His claims about the Nord Stream sabotage and Ukraine's ability to repay its loans were not independently established by the remarks themselves.
